name: Vael Passionfruit-Mate
description: A naturally caffeinated sparkling drink combining passionfruit flavor with real yerba mate extract, positioned as a 'clean energy' alternative to synthetic stimulant drinks. Popular with Tier 2-3 knowledge workers, students, and anyone who needs focus without chrome.
flavor_profile: Tropical passionfruit sweetness layered over mate's earthy, slightly bitter green undertone, dry finish, medium carbonation with a persistent mild caffeine warmth
cultural_context: Vael occupies the functional beverage niche — marketed to people who distrust synthetic stimulant compounds but can't afford premium nootropics. It's the drink of the perpetually deadline-pressured: BCI interface technicians, mid-tier coders, transit dispatchers. 'Running on Vael' is slang for operating at sustainable-but-not-peak capacity.
story_hooks: Vael's 'real yerba mate extract' is real — but sourced from a controlled agricultural zone with contested land rights, and an activist cell wants to attach a boycott to the brand.

A Tier 2 student has discovered that Vael interacts with a specific budget BCI implant model to enhance focus beyond normal parameters — not marketed, not tested, potentially dangerous, and spreading as a study hack.

A Vael delivery route in the industrial district has been rerouted three times in a month — someone is intercepting specific pallet numbers, and the manifest discrepancies don't match any known theft pattern.
